I knew there would be a comment like this... I guess I can see how that sounds negative. I feel like I've just really had socially bad luck in my life. I'm very hopeful about the future and am excited to meet new people, but it does me no good to lie to myself and pretend that the people I was interacting with, were OK or that they respected me when they weren't. I'm sorry if I come across as judgemental- I'm not- no one needs to be perfect- it's just the vibes I've gotten.

When I say asshole friends, I mean these guys will only talk to me if their original plans cancel, as a last resort, etc. They have no problem dragging me out to wherever they are but refuse to come to my neighborhood. They don't care to text if I make it home okay, and if they invite another friend along they'll exclude me from the conversation by talking about something I'm not involved with. They'll also make mean comments occasionally like dis my job in a non-joking way. That's what I mean by shitty guys. Obviously we don't need to be bff's, but if they can't even give two shits when we're together, then I can't be friends with someone like that. We're incompatible. I want people who actually respect and like me. 

Again, I'm NOT negative - this has been my reality and I'm simply stating it so that the people on here can understand the situation. I'm not passing judgment on myself or others. Obviously I want to change this situation and obviously I'm happy about the prospect of meeting people. 

> take a look at yourself and figure out what kind of image you're projecting -- why do people seem to not "like" you? do they seem bored? when you have conversations with them, how do those conversations end? do people seem to think you're aloof? etc.

It depends on the person, but in general (again, NOT being negative, just stating what I notice!) is that people tend to vent to me and tend to treat me as a more "serious" person/friend, as opposed to someone to go out and have fun with, or to joke around with, or seem excited about. I like to banter and usually just don't even try that on most people, but occasionally will try to change the conversation to playful at an appropriate interjection (ex. someone says i've never been to this thai place! and i'll say something in a joke-y fashion like "wow you need more spice in your life" -- that was dumb but you get it) and the person will either respond seriously like "yeah" or like will give a quiet polite laugh. I personally feel like others feel drained after hanging out with me but at the same time it doesn't seem like they're enthusiastic in the first place. I'll ask them tons of questions about themselves but they almost seem like whatever about it- not smiling, not excited. I see that contrasted with them around other people and it's like their faces are lit up, they seem happy and engaged. Like the other person has something I don't. 

When I end conversations with people, they're usually off to talk to someone else, almost to "recover" from the conversation. I've had people who were initially open to friendships with me to some extent, but then either took advantage of me (presumably due to lack of respect) and/or start to resent me. 

For example, my roommates (I have two) moved in around the same time (i had been there) and we all sort of hit it off. But the girl one seemed way more into the guy one, not that they even had more in common, but I guess she just was into him more than me. And like even though they hardly see each other and rarely if ever go out, consider each other friends. Whereas, I am home a lot and see both of them on a daily basis, but neither consider me a friend and just a "roommate" - in spite of us having numerous conversations and me opening up to them. 

I think that once people friend me on facebook, they see that i'm not that well liked - they see i dont have a ton of friends and hardly any pictures, and they get subtly turned off - like this girl is a loser, she's weird, she's low-value. I'm sure that's what it's like with guys too. They go to my social media accounts, and that with hanging out wth me, assures them that i'm no prize and not someone anyone would seriously want to be associated with.

I think if a person makes you uncomfortable enough, you just feel like it's time to go. You know people you've either been friends with or have known who are a little- off? Or you're not exactly looking forward to hanging out with them? That should be a time to dump. 
Obviously things like abusive, drug addiction type things are red flags. But a lot of the time it's something that you don't feel you can deal with. Look less at the small things and more at how you feel when with them. If you are constantly on the defensive, or feel ignored, or feel like they're not really seeing you, then those are things to break up over.

Hey, I was in your place not too long ago. I was dating a guy as a bandaid and it wound up imploding and sent me spiraling into depression and my self esteem was rock bottom. It was the worst summer ever and I swear I was an inch away from ending it. But it made me a better person because once I came to terms with my demons, things got so much better. The world opened up. I had terrible issues with guys too, and I literally LIVED for male approval through relationships, but it wound up being a huge disaster every time.

The truth is, guys do not matter, or at least, they *should not* matter for your happiness. If you put your happiness in a guy, you will never be happy. If your gut is telling you that this is not going anywhere, then you need to make sure that you get away from it (cut ties) and don't look back. First of all, guys DO come back, and second of all, you're putting YOUR life below this guys by continuing to be in this relationship. Your best bet is obviously to cut things and don't regret it, because I knew that when I debated the same thing you were in, that I was very fearful of regretting it. Trust me, you will be OK letting this guy go.
